requirements.original: A host id can be used to give a specific deployment location to the test system where the MTC shall be started and execute its behaviour.
requirements.canonical: If a host id is given in an `execute` statement, the MTC SHALL be started and execute its behaviour on the deployment location identified by the host id.
requirements.condition: a host id is provided in the execute statement

examples.text:
v_myVerdict := execute(TC_MyTestCase3(), -, "Host1");
  // executes TC_MyTestCase3 with unlimited time with MTC deployed to 'Host1'

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- A host id can be used to give a specific deployment location to the test system where the MTC shall be started and execute its behaviour.

requirements.original: If a host id is provided, the execute statement shall end with a test case error if the MTC cannot be deployed on the specified host.
requirements.canonical: If a host id is provided and the MTC cannot be deployed on the specified host, the `execute` statement SHALL end with a test case error.
requirements.condition: a host id is provided and the MTC cannot be deployed on the specified host
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- If a host id is provided, the execute statement shall end with a test case error if the MTC cannot be deployed on the specified host.

requirements.original: a) The TimerValue shall resolve to a non-negative numerical float value (i.e. the value shall be greater or equal 0.0, infinity and not_a_number are disallowed).
requirements.canonical: The TimerValue of an `execute` statement SHALL resolve to a non-negative `float` value (greater than or equal to 0.0).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- a) The TimerValue shall resolve to a non-negative numerical float value (i.e. the value shall be greater or equal 0.0, infinity and not_a_number are disallowed).

requirements.original: a) The TimerValue shall resolve to a non-negative numerical float value (i.e. the value shall be greater or equal 0.0, infinity and not_a_number are disallowed).
requirements.canonical: The TimerValue of an `execute` statement SHALL NOT resolve to `infinity` or `not_a_number`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- a) The TimerValue shall resolve to a non-negative numerical float value (i.e. the value shall be greater or equal 0.0, infinity and not_a_number are disallowed).

requirements.original: b) When the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type TemplateInstance shall resolve to an _Expression._ c) The execute statement shall not be called from within an existing executing test behaviour chain called from a test case, i.e. test cases can only be executed from a control behaviour.
requirements.canonical: If the corresponding formal parameter is not of template kind, an actual parameter (TemplateInstance) of an `execute` statement SHALL resolve to an expression.
requirements.condition: the corresponding formal parameter of the test case is not a template parameter

ambiguity.issue: The grammar symbol TemplateInstance is used where the actual parameter is meant (the syntax block uses ActualPar); "of template type" means a template formal parameter, not a type.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- b) When the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type TemplateInstance shall resolve to an _Expression._ c) The execute statement shall not be called from within an existing executing test behaviour chain called from a test case, i.e. test cases can only be executed from a control behaviour.

requirements.original: b) When the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type TemplateInstance shall resolve to an _Expression._ c) The execute statement shall not be called from within an existing executing test behaviour chain called from a test case, i.e. test cases can only be executed from a control behaviour.
requirements.canonical: The `execute` statement SHALL NOT be called from within a test behaviour called from a test case; a test case SHALL only be executed from control behaviour.

ambiguity.issue: "executing test behaviour chain" is not a defined term; the call chain of functions and altsteps started by a test case (test behaviour) is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- b) When the corresponding formal parameter is not of template type TemplateInstance shall resolve to an _Expression._ c) The execute statement shall not be called from within an existing executing test behaviour chain called from a test case, i.e. test cases can only be executed from a control behaviour.

requirements.original: d) The HostId parameter shall resolve to a charstring value.
requirements.canonical: The HostId parameter of an `execute` statement SHALL resolve to a `charstring` value.

examples.text:
v_myVerdict := execute(TC_MyTestCase3(), -, "Host1");
  // executes TC_MyTestCase3 with unlimited time with MTC deployed to 'Host1'

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.1 -- d) The HostId parameter shall resolve to a charstring value.

requirements.original: The module control function defines, in which order, sequence, loop, under which preconditions, and with which parameters test cases are to be executed.
requirements.canonical: The module control function defines the order, sequence, loops, preconditions and actual parameters with which test cases are executed.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- The module control function defines, in which order, sequence, loop, under which preconditions, and with which parameters test cases are to be executed.

requirements.original: The module control function is an entry point for execution of a TTCN-3 test suite.
requirements.canonical: The module control function IS an entry point for the execution of a TTCN-3 test suite.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- The module control function is an entry point for execution of a TTCN-3 test suite.

requirements.original: If the function contains formal parameters, their actual values shall be provided.
requirements.canonical: If the module control function has formal parameters, actual values SHALL be provided for them when the module control function is executed.
requirements.condition: the module control function has formal parameters
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- If the function contains formal parameters, their actual values shall be provided.

requirements.original: When the control function is started, the TE creates a test component called control component.
requirements.canonical: When the module control function is started, the test system creates a test component called control component.

ambiguity.issue: The abbreviation "TE" (TTCN-3 executable) is not defined in the core language; "test system" is the glossary term. "control function" means the module control function.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- When the control function is started, the TE creates a test component called control component.

requirements.original: The created control component is of the type specified in the runs `on clause of the` module control function.
requirements.canonical: The control component IS of the component type specified in the `runs on` clause of the module control function.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- The created control component is of the type specified in the runs `on clause of the` module control function.

requirements.original: If the runs `on clause is missing, an empty control component is created.`
requirements.canonical: If the module control function has no `runs on` clause, an empty control component IS created.
requirements.condition: the module control function has no runs on clause
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- If the runs `on clause is missing, an empty control component is created.`

requirements.original: Program statements specify such things like the order in which test cases are to be executed or the number of times a test case should run.
requirements.canonical: Program statements in the module control function CAN specify the order in which test cases are executed and the number of times a test case runs.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- Program statements specify such things like the order in which test cases are to be executed or the number of times a test case should run.

requirements.original: If no programming statements are used then, by default, the test cases are executed in the sequential order in which they appear in the module control function.
requirements.canonical: If no program statements are used, test cases ARE executed by default in the sequential order in which they appear in the module control function.

ambiguity.issue: The module control function needs execute statements, so "no programming statements" most likely means no control-flow statements; reading chosen: execute statements without control-flow statements run in textual order.
readings: If the module control function contains no control-flow statements, its `execute` statements ARE executed in textual order.
If the module control function contains no statements other than test case references, the referenced test cases ARE executed in textual order.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- If no programming statements are used then, by default, the test cases are executed in the sequential order in which they appear in the module control function.

requirements.original: Timer operations may also be used explicitly to control test case execution.
requirements.canonical: A timer operation MAY be used explicitly in the module control function to control test case execution.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- Timer operations may also be used explicitly to control test case execution.

requirements.original: For example, boolean expressions may be used to select and deselect which test cases are to be executed.
requirements.canonical: A boolean expression MAY be used in the module control function to select or deselect test cases for execution.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- For example, boolean expressions may be used to select and deselect which test cases are to be executed.

requirements.original: This includes, of course, the use of functions that return a boolean value.
requirements.canonical: A function returning a `boolean` value MAY be used in the module control function to select or deselect test cases for execution.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- This includes, of course, the use of functions that return a boolean value.

requirements.original: Another way to execute test cases as a group is to collect them in a control function and invoke that function from the module control function.
requirements.canonical: Test cases MAY be executed as a group by collecting their `execute` statements in a function that is invoked from the module control function.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- Another way to execute test cases as a group is to collect them in a control function and invoke that function from the module control function.

requirements.original: As a test case returns a single value of type verdicttype, it is also possible to control the order of test case execution depending on the outcome of a test case.
requirements.canonical: The module control function CAN make the order of test case execution depend on the `verdicttype` value returned by a test case.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- As a test case returns a single value of type verdicttype, it is also possible to control the order of test case execution depending on the outcome of a test case.

requirements.original: The use of the TTCN-3 verdicttype is another way to select test cases.
requirements.canonical: A `verdicttype` value returned by an `execute` statement MAY be used to select test cases for execution.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 26.2 -- The use of the TTCN-3 verdicttype is another way to select test cases.

requirements.original: Attributes can be associated with TTCN-3 language elements by means of the with statement.
requirements.canonical: An attribute MAY be associated with a TTCN-3 language element by means of the `with` statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.0 -- Attributes can be associated with TTCN-3 language elements by means of the with statement.

requirements.original: The with statement can be applied to modules, global module definitions and to local definitions in control, test cases, functions, altsteps, statement blocks and in component type definitions.
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement MAY be applied to a module, to a global module definition, and to a local definition in the module control function, in a test case, in a function, in an altstep, in a statement block or in a component type definition.

ambiguity.issue: 'control' is used for the module control function; the outdated term 'control part' is implied.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.0 -- The with statement can be applied to modules, global module definitions and to local definitions in control, test cases, functions, altsteps, statement blocks and in component type definitions.

requirements.original: A with statement may associate attributes to a single language element
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement MAY associate attributes to a single language element.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.1 -- A with statement may associate attributes to a single language element

requirements.original: or to elements or fields of structured types (in a recursive way) ... the same way as specified in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.3.2.
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement MAY associate attributes, recursively, to fields or elements of a structured type, in the same way as specified in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.3.2.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.1 -- or to elements or fields of structured types (in a recursive way) ... the same way as specified in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.3.2.

requirements.original: or to members of component or port types, the same way as specified in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.3.2.
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement MAY associate attributes to members of a component type or a port type, in the same way as specified in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.3.2.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.1 -- or to members of component or port types, the same way as specified in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.3.2.

requirements.original: It is also possible to associate attributes to a number of language elements by, e.g. listing fields of a structured type in an attribute statement associated with a single type definition
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement associated with a single structured type definition MAY associate attributes to several fields of that type by listing the fields in the attribute statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.1 -- It is also possible to associate attributes to a number of language elements by, e.g. listing fields of a structured type in an attribute statement associated with a single type definition

requirements.original: or associating a with statement to the surrounding scope unit or group of language elements.
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement associated with a surrounding scope unit or a group MAY associate attributes to all language elements of that scope unit or group.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.1 -- or associating a with statement to the surrounding scope unit or group of language elements.

requirements.original: A with statement can follow any module, any global definition inside module and group declarations as well as any local definition in component types and statement blocks inside behaviour definitions.
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement MAY follow any module, any global definition inside module and group declarations, and any local definition in component types and in statement blocks inside behaviour definitions.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.1 -- A with statement can follow any module, any global definition inside module and group declarations as well as any local definition in component types and statement blocks inside behaviour definitions.

requirements.original: Attributes can be attached to synonym types (clause 6.4).
requirements.canonical: An attribute MAY be attached to a synonym type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.1 -- Attributes can be attached to synonym types (clause 6.4).

requirements.original: If the synonym type is a structured type, attributes in the with statement may reference fields or elements of this structured type.
requirements.canonical: If a synonym type is a structured type, the attributes in the `with` statement of the synonym type MAY reference fields or elements of that structured type.
requirements.condition: the synonym type is a structured type
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.1 -- If the synonym type is a structured type, attributes in the with statement may reference fields or elements of this structured type.

requirements.original: An attribute definition that is directly attached to a lower scope unit will override a general attribute definition in a higher scope
requirements.canonical: An attribute definition that is directly attached to a lower scope unit IS overriding a general attribute definition of a higher scope.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- An attribute definition that is directly attached to a lower scope unit will override a general attribute definition in a higher scope

requirements.original: An attribute definition that is directly attached to a lower scope unit will override ... a type-specific attribute inherited from a type reference.
requirements.canonical: An attribute definition that is directly attached to a lower scope unit IS overriding a type-specific attribute inherited from a type reference.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- An attribute definition that is directly attached to a lower scope unit will override ... a type-specific attribute inherited from a type reference.

requirements.original: Attributes inherited from a type reference will override general attributes from a higher scope unit containing the type reference.
requirements.canonical: An attribute inherited from a type reference IS overriding a general attribute of a higher scope unit that contains the type reference.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- Attributes inherited from a type reference will override general attributes from a higher scope unit containing the type reference.

requirements.original: A with statement that is placed inside the scope of another with statement shall override the outermost with.
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement that is placed inside the scope of another `with` statement SHALL override the outer `with` statement.

ambiguity.issue: 'the outermost with' can be read literally (only the outermost of several nested with statements) or as 'any enclosing with'. The second reading is chosen because the nested overriding scheme of example 2 implies it.
readings: A `with` statement that is placed inside the scope of another `with` statement SHALL override every enclosing `with` statement.
A `with` statement that is placed inside the scope of another `with` statement SHALL override only the outermost `with` statement.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- A with statement that is placed inside the scope of another with statement shall override the outermost with.

requirements.original: This shall also apply to the use of the with statement with groups.
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement associated with a group nested inside another group SHALL override the `with` statement of the enclosing group.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- This shall also apply to the use of the with statement with groups.

requirements.original: If multiple attributes of the same type are allowed, all of them are overridden unless specified otherwise.
requirements.canonical: If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed, an overriding attribute definition IS overriding all of the attributes of that kind, unless specified otherwise.
requirements.condition: multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed

ambiguity.issue: 'unless specified otherwise' does not say where the exception is specified (e.g. clause 27.1.2.2 for multiple encodings); 'type' is used for the kind of attribute. Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed, an overriding attribute definition IS overriding all of them, except where another clause of the standard specifies a different rule.
If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed, an overriding attribute definition IS overriding all of them, unless the overriding attribute definition itself specifies otherwise.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- If multiple attributes of the same type are allowed, all of them are overridden unless specified otherwise.

requirements.original: Attributes defined for a synonym type do not override existing attributes of fields or elements of this synonym type.
requirements.canonical: An attribute defined for a synonym type IS NOT overriding an existing attribute of a field or element of the synonym type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- Attributes defined for a synonym type do not override existing attributes of fields or elements of this synonym type.

requirements.original: The attributes are applied to the fields or elements of synonym types only if the fields or elements have no valid attributes.
requirements.canonical: An attribute of a synonym type IS applied to a field or element of the synonym type only if the field or element has no valid attribute.
requirements.condition: the field or element has no valid attribute
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- The attributes are applied to the fields or elements of synonym types only if the fields or elements have no valid attributes.

requirements.original: Attributes with the @local modifier override attributes from higher scope
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `@local` modifier IS overriding attributes from a higher scope.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- Attributes with the @local modifier override attributes from higher scope

requirements.original: but they are valid for the associated language element only.
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `@local` modifier IS valid for the associated language element only.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- but they are valid for the associated language element only.

requirements.original: They do not affect definitions inside the associated language element as the @local attribute is completely transparent to lower scopes.
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `@local` modifier IS NOT affecting definitions inside the associated language element, because it is transparent to lower scopes.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- They do not affect definitions inside the associated language element as the @local attribute is completely transparent to lower scopes.

requirements.original: Attributes from higher scope will still affect attributes in lower scopes even if the @local attribute is between them.
requirements.canonical: An attribute from a higher scope IS affecting the language elements of lower scopes even if an attribute with the `@local` modifier is attached to a scope between them.

ambiguity.issue: 'affect attributes in lower scopes' is read as affecting the language elements of lower scopes (they inherit the higher-scope attribute), not as modifying explicit lower-scope attributes.
readings: An attribute from a higher scope IS applied to the language elements of lower scopes even if an attribute with the `@local` modifier is attached to an intermediate scope.
An attribute from a higher scope IS overriding explicitly declared attributes in lower scopes even if an attribute with the `@local` modifier is attached to an intermediate scope.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- Attributes from higher scope will still affect attributes in lower scopes even if the @local attribute is between them.

requirements.original: NOTE: Attributes with the @local modifier associated to modules and groups are valid
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `@local` modifier associated with a module or a group IS valid.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- NOTE: Attributes with the @local modifier associated to modules and groups are valid

requirements.original: but do not affect the definitions inside them.
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `@local` modifier associated with a module or a group IS NOT affecting the definitions inside the module or group.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- but do not affect the definitions inside them.

requirements.original: An attribute definition in a lower scope or those inherited from a referenced type can be overwritten in a higher scope by using the override directive.
requirements.canonical: An attribute definition in a lower scope, or an attribute inherited from a referenced type, MAY be overwritten from a higher scope by using the `override` directive.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- An attribute definition in a lower scope or those inherited from a referenced type can be overwritten in a higher scope by using the override directive.

requirements.original: The override directive overrides the specified attribute for all declarations at all lower scopes that do not also declare the specified attribute.
requirements.canonical: The `override` directive IS overriding the specified attribute for all declarations at all lower scopes that do not also declare the specified attribute.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence seems to conflict with 27.1.2.0-s022, which states that the override directive overwrites attribute definitions of lower scopes. Example 6 (MyRecordD.fieldC keeps RuleC against the group's override RuleA) suggests that a lower declaration with its own override directive is kept. Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: The `override` directive IS overriding the specified attribute for all lower-scope declarations, except those lower-scope declarations that declare the same attribute with an `override` directive themselves.
The `override` directive IS overriding the specified attribute only for lower-scope declarations that do not declare the specified attribute at all.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- The override directive overrides the specified attribute for all declarations at all lower scopes that do not also declare the specified attribute.

requirements.original: If the override directive is applied to a type reference, it does not affect the attributes of the original referenced type.
requirements.canonical: If the `override` directive is applied to a type reference, the `override` directive IS NOT affecting the attributes of the original referenced type.
requirements.condition: the override directive is applied to a type reference
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- If the override directive is applied to a type reference, it does not affect the attributes of the original referenced type.

requirements.original: An attribute definition directly attached to a field or element of a structured type overrides the corresponding attribute of the structured type, as regards the identified field or element.
requirements.canonical: An attribute definition directly attached to a field or element of a structured type IS overriding the corresponding attribute of the structured type for the identified field or element.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- An attribute definition directly attached to a field or element of a structured type overrides the corresponding attribute of the structured type, as regards the identified field or element.

requirements.original: Override attribute applied to a synonym type (clause 6.4) overrides attributes of all fields or elements of the synonym type unless the synonym type definition contains an explicit attribute definition for the field or element.
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `override` directive applied to a synonym type IS overriding the attributes of all fields or elements of the synonym type, unless the synonym type definition contains an explicit attribute definition for the field or element.

ambiguity.issue: 'Override attribute' is used for an attribute carrying the override directive.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 27.1.2.0 -- Override attribute applied to a synonym type (clause 6.4) overrides attributes of all fields or elements of the synonym type unless the synonym type definition contains an explicit attribute definition for the field or element.
